text: “Their uncle must do the preventing. He must take them away.” “And who’s to make him?” She had been scanning the distance, but she now dropped on me a foolish face. “You, miss.” “By writing to him that his house is poisoned and his little nephew and niece mad?” “But if they are, miss?” “And if I am myself, you mean? That’s charming news to be sent him by a governess whose prime undertaking was to give him no worry.” Mrs. Grose considered, following the children again. “Yes, he do hate worry.
